title: Add a defaults entry: criteria check behavior, protections tested as roo
summary: Add a new entry to defaults.toml (applies to all work) saying every acceptance criterion must check the requested behavior happening, and that protection or denial tests must first show the action succeeds unprotected as the real user (root), then is refused, and fail rather than skip if the environment cannot enforce it. Add worked examples for 'make X read-only' and 'role calls a model' requests. The audience is the reader, producer and verifier, who receive the rendered defaults.

defaults_applied.how: The rule is enforced by a unit test that the entry exists and renders its core sentence, not left as prose.
Add a defaults.rs test; cargo test and clippy stay clean.
Behavior criteria are checked by running cargo test.
One new default plus tests and examples, with no reader logic changes.
The statement and examples are written for an outside reader.
The docs example cites the source request and the defaults-loop design.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: 'Reading default' means a new entry in defaults.toml that the reader cites in defaults_applied; it is not a code change to the reader's logic.
The new entry applies_to ["*"] because the rule concerns acceptance criteria for any class of work.
'Show that a reading ... produces criteria of this form' is satisfied by worked examples in docs plus tests that the rendered default carries the rule; Athena cannot run the reader live from tests.
The existing render() only emits the first sentence, so the core rule must lead the statement; the root-user and fail-not-skip details stay in the full statement text.
The verifier's allowed commands run as the real component's user, so examples cite cargo test as the way to check.

acceptance_criteria.text: defaults.toml has a new [[default]] entry (for example id "behavior-evidence") with applies_to ["*"], a source citing this request, and a statement whose FIRST sentence states the core rule (criteria check the requested behavior happening, not that types, files or wiring exist), because the rendered brief shows only the first sentence.

The statement's later sentences require that any protection/denial test first shows the action succeeds without the protection, under the same user and environment the real component runs as (root), then shows it is refused, and that if the environment cannot enforce the protection the test fails rather than skips or passes silently.

A new unit test in crates/athena-data/src/defaults.rs parses the repository defaults.toml and asserts the new entry exists and its render() line appears with the core rule; run `cargo test -p athena-data` and see it pass, while existing tests (including root_cause_default_leads_with_the_core_rule) still pass.

A worked example (docs/design/defaults-loop.md or a doc test fixture) shows a reading for 'make X read-only' whose criteria are: (1) a write to X as root succeeds before protection, (2) after protection the same write as root is refused, (3) the test fails, not skips, if the environment cannot enforce it (e.g. a root-bypassed file mode is not accepted as proof).

A second worked example for 'role calls a model' has criteria that run the role end to end and check the model call is made and its output is used (for example through the fake client, with the request observed), not merely that a client type or config is wired in.
`cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo fmt --check` all pass from the repository root.

out_of_scope: Changing how the reader, producer or verifier prompts are built beyond the existing defaults rendering
Implementing an actual read-only protection or model-calling role
